clarifications: Mitotic recombination refers to cycling cells; DNA repair can precede the next mitosis.
Remove the unsupported universal once-per-million upper limit. Rates depend on assay and context.
LOH is an allelic-state change, not necessarily chromosome loss; the illustrated crossover outcome is conditional on segregation.
Cancer and clone-growth examples describe possibilities, not inevitable outcomes.
Mitotic crossover can occur spontaneously; DNA breaks can arise during ordinary cell activity. An experimental damage treatment is not required.
DNA-copying or break repair can lead to exchange; using a matching DNA copy is not itself a crossover. Do not claim one initiating lesion explains every spontaneous event.
Meiotic recombination also begins with controlled DNA breaks. This is instructor context, not a new repair-pathway lesson.
Explain daughter cells and patches before naming loss of heterozygosity. Keep the two chromosome-separation outcomes visible.

Controlled DNA cleavage starts meiotic recombination; instructor background for the distinction between a DNA break and an unnatural event.
